title: Noetherianity and coherence of invertible modules on a proper scheme over a field
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field], let $Y$ be a scheme proper over $k$ [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $\mathcal N$ be an invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module [def-sc-invertible-module]. Then $Y$ is Noetherian, meaning locally Noetherian [pqf-def-locnoeth] and quasi-compact [def-weil-pbc-quasi-compact-scheme], and $\mathcal N$ and $\mathcal O_Y$ are coherent $\mathcal O_Y$-modules [pqf-def-coherent]. No dimension, reducedness or connectedness hypothesis on $Y$ is imposed.

proof.text: Every ideal of $k$ is either zero or all of $k$: an ideal containing $a\ne0$ contains $a^{-1}a=1$. These ideals are generated by the empty set and by $1$, respectively, so $k$ is Noetherian. The one affine chart $\operatorname{Spec}k$, with ring of sections $k$, is therefore a Noetherian affine cover of $\operatorname{Spec}k$; thus this base is locally Noetherian.

source.place: Tag 01OV, definition-noetherian; the field ideal argument is written out

proof.text: Write $f:Y\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ for the structure morphism. Properness gives separatedness and finite type, hence locally finite type and quasi-compactness. Apply [pqf-lem-locnoeth-lft] with the locally Noetherian base of Step 1 to obtain that $Y$ is locally Noetherian. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-over-affine] to $f$, whose target is affine and which is separated and of finite type, to obtain that $Y$ is quasi-compact. These are exactly the two required Noetherianity conditions.

By [def-sc-invertible-module], $\mathcal N$ is quasi-coherent and has a Zariski cover on which $\mathcal N|_U\simeq\mathcal O_U$. On each such open the inverse of this isomorphism is a surjection $\mathcal O_U^{\oplus1}\to\mathcal N|_U$. This is precisely finite type in [pqf-def-coherent]. Also $\mathcal O_Y$ is of finite type using its identity map. It is quasi-coherent: every point lies in an affine open $U$ with $(U,\mathcal O_Y|_U)\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], so it suffices to show $\mathcal O_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\cong\widetilde A$. Take $\widetilde A$ and the maps $\tau_V:A\to\widetilde A(V)$ of [lem-weil-pbc-spec-module-tilde-sections] with module $N=A$. Define $\varphi_V:\mathcal O(V)\to\widetilde A(V)$ by $\varphi_V(s)=s\cdot\tau_V(1)$. It is $\mathcal O$-linear, and it commutes with restriction because $\tau$ does and the module action is compatible with restriction. On $D(r)$ that lemma identifies $\widetilde A(D(r))$ with $A_r$, with the natural $\mathcal O(D(r))=A_r$-module structure and $\tau_{D(r)}(1)=1/1$. Hence $\varphi_{D(r)}(a/r^k)=a/r^k$, so $\varphi_{D(r)}$ is bijective. The opens $D(r)$ form a basis, and every stalk is the colimit over basic neighbourhoods. Hence $\varphi$ is bijective on all stalks and is an isomorphism of sheaves. Thus both modules are quasi-coherent of finite type.

proof.text: Apply the implication from quasi-coherent of finite type to coherent in [pqf-lem-coherent-ft-locnoeth], on the locally Noetherian scheme $Y$ of Step 2, first to $\mathcal N$ and then to $\mathcal O_Y$, using Step 3. This proves both coherence assertions. Neither application needs a dimension, reducedness or connectedness assumption.
